summary: McKean County tower on Mt. Beacon, planned at eighty feet in 1931 and open for the 1935 fall season; no later source found.

events.note: April 1931 reports describe the tower as being erected, planned at eighty feet; the finished height is not recorded.
Opened for the fall season as the observation point for the northern fire district; Mr. Coleman reported on the woods.
Telephone service to be installed in the tower under the association's sponsorship.

evidence.supports: Page names the site MT. BEACON (Hehge hog)
April 1931: planned eighty-foot tower on Mt. Beacon, highest point in that section of the county
evidence.quote: It will be an eighty foot tower and will be erected on Mt. Beacon, the highest point in that section of the county

evidence.supports: Tower being erected and paid for by the McKean County Protective Fire Association
evidence.quote: This tower is being erected and paid for entirely by the McKean County Protective Fire Association

evidence.supports: Northwest portion of the county was the only section not properly protected from forest fires
evidence.quote: the only section which is not properly protected from forest fires

evidence.supports: Planned new road from the Bennett Brook road to the tower site, for a view of the county from the top
evidence.quote: construction of a new and better road from the Bennett Brook road to the site of this tower in order that they may get a view of McKean County from the top of the structure

evidence.supports: Airway beacon planned for the top at some later date
evidence.quote: with an air-way beacon upon which it is the plan of the Harri Emery Airport Association to place a beacon at some future date

evidence.supports: Tower to be named by schoolchildren from Bradford and nearby townships
evidence.quote: will be known by a name to be selected by the school children of the city of Bradford, the townships of Croydon, Foster, Bradford, Otto, Keating, Lafayette and Hamilton

evidence.supports: 1935 item: observation point for the northern fire district of McKean County
evidence.quote: Mt Beacon fire tower observation point for the northern fire district of McKean county

evidence.supports: 1935 item: tower less than two miles west of Bradford; opened for the fall season
evidence.quote: located less than two miles west of Bradford, opened for the fall season this morning.

evidence.supports: Forest pronounced unusually dry in October 1935
evidence.quote: Although the forest is pronounced unusually dry

evidence.supports: Opening was at least two weeks later than in many previous years
evidence.quote: opening of the tower is at least two weeks later than many in previous years

evidence.supports: Mr. Coleman reported no fires discovered in the woods yet
evidence.quote: Mr. Coleman reported there have been no fires discovered in the woods yet.

evidence.supports: Telephone service to be installed in the tower under the association's sponsorship
evidence.quote: Telephone service will be installed in the tower today under the sponsorship of the McKean County Protective Fire Association.

evidence.supports: April 23 item gives the association as the McKean Protective Fire Association
evidence.quote: This tower is being erected and paid for entirely by the McKean Protective Fire Association

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 16 April 1931 item names the McKean County Protective Fire Association; the 23 April item shortens it to McKean Protective Fire Association. The story uses the fuller name, which the 1935 item also gives.

notes_for_editor: Single source: one page of 1931 and 1935 newspaper extracts. No register entry in the NHLR or FFLOS caches. The page header says Hehge hog, which may be a misspelling of Hedgehog; not verified. Do not use hvmag.com (2013 article on a Mt. Beacon fire tower in Beacon, Dutchess County, NY), which is a different tower. height_m is the planned 80 ft (24.4 m) from 1931 reports, not a confirmed built height. The agency key is the sponsoring association from the 1931 and 1935 items, not a confirmed managing agency. No status, access or later history found in two searches.
